items.question: Under what condition must a certain teaching be concealed rather than openly disclosed in the mortal world?
premises: A teaching is to be concealed with effort.
This concealment is prescribed for the mortal world.
It is prescribed specifically among the lowest of men.
items.inference: The teaching requires guarded concealment in the mortal sphere, particularly among the lowest of men.
items.plain_english: It must be concealed with effort in the mortal world, among the lowest of men.

rows.grounds: compound analyzed as member+membership; tested over one year

items.question: What qualification must a previously accomplished person meet before a certain gift is to be given to him?
premises: A gift is to be given to a previously accomplished person.
That person must have been tested for one year.
The test of one year is a condition for the giving.
items.inference: The gift is to be given only to a previously accomplished person who has been tested for one year.
items.plain_english: It is to be given to one previously accomplished who has been tested for one year.

items.question: What numerical position does the chapter hold that has emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: A chapter has emerged from Candradvīpa.
That chapter is designated as the fifth.
Its designation is paṭala.
items.inference: The chapter that emerged from Candradvīpa is the fifth chapter.
items.plain_english: The fifth chapter is the one that emerged from Candradvīpa.

rows.grounds: instrumental compound of tvat and prasāda
nominative compound of kaula and nirṇaya

items.question: By what means does the speaker come to know the determination of the Kaula doctrine?
premises: The speaker addresses the Lord of the Kaulas.
By the grace of that Lord, the speaker has come to know.
What is known is the determination of the Kaula doctrine.
items.inference: Through the grace of the Lord of the Kaulas, the speaker has come to know the determination of the Kaula doctrine.
items.plain_english: By your grace, O Lord of the Kaulas, I have come to know the determination of the Kaula doctrine.

rows.grounds: nominative compound of jīva and svarūpa

items.question: What two points of inquiry are raised concerning the soul and its nature?
premises: A question is raised as to which soul is declared.
A further question is raised as to what the nature of the soul is.
The two inquiries stand as alternatives.
items.inference: The inquiry concerns both which soul is declared and what the nature of the soul is.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that is declared? Or what is the nature of the soul?

rows.grounds: locative of ka/im; fused form as given
nominative compound of tat and sarva

items.question: What request is made concerning the locus of dissolution and the totality of what dissolves there?
premises: A question is asked in which thing dissolution indeed occurs.
A request is made to tell all of that to the speaker.
The inquiry links the locus of dissolution to that totality.
items.inference: The speaker requests to be told in what dissolution occurs and all that belongs to that matter.
items.plain_english: And in what indeed does it go to dissolution? Tell me all of that.

rows.grounds: accusative compound of nirāmaya and nirañjana

items.question: What set of attributes is ascribed to that which is spoken of as supreme?
premises: That is designated as supreme.
That is designated as partless and eternal.
That is designated as free from disease and stainless.
items.inference: That supreme reality is partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless.
items.plain_english: He is the supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease and stainless.

rows.grounds: nominative compound of śakti and pudgala

items.question: What identity is established between the soul, the Haṃsa, and the power-individual?
premises: He is the soul and the more supreme one.
He who is that is indeed the Haṃsa.
He is the power-individual.
items.inference: The soul who is the more supreme is identical with the Haṃsa, who is the power-individual.
items.plain_english: He is the soul, the more supreme one; he indeed is the Haṃsa, the power-individual.

rows.grounds: nominative compound of samīra and pūraka
locative compound of sarva and jīva

items.question: Where is the wind-filling air situated according to this statement?
premises: The air is wind-filling.
That air is situated in all beings.
Its presence is stated as situated within them.
items.inference: The wind-filling air is situated in all beings.
items.plain_english: The wind-filling air is situated in all beings.

rows.grounds: instrumental compound of deha, tyakta, mātra

items.question: Under what minimal condition is that person called the supreme Śiva?
premises: Upon merely leaving the body, a change of state occurs.
At that point he is called the supreme Śiva.
The designation follows from that minimal condition.
items.inference: Upon merely leaving the body, he is called the supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: Upon merely leaving the body, he is called the supreme Śiva.

rows.grounds: nominative/accusative compound of karṇa and stha
nominative compound of pāramparya, krama, āgata

items.question: What kind of teaching is heard abiding in the ear, and by what mode of transmission does it come?
premises: A teaching abiding in the ear is heard.
This is addressed to the Goddess.
That teaching has come down through a traditional order.
items.inference: What abides in the ear and is heard, O Goddess, is a teaching that has come down through tradition in order.
items.plain_english: It is heard abiding in the ear, O Goddess, as it has come down through the traditional order.

rows.grounds: instrumental compound of jñāna and mātra

items.question: By what means is a certain result attained, as addressed to the fair-faced one?
premises: Attainment is said to occur by this means.
That means is mere knowledge.
It is also said to occur by what has been heard.
items.inference: By mere knowledge and by what has been heard, attainment occurs, O fair-faced one.
items.plain_english: By this mere knowledge, and by what has been heard, O fair-faced one.
